title: Inferring constitutive forces from noisy Allen-Cahn movies with moment equations
abstract: Inferring an Allen-Cahn constitutive force from images requires more than an accurate optimizer: nonlinear observation noise alters the mean of force features, shared noise couples instruments to the response, and a temporal balance borrowed from another solver can remain biased even on clean data. We develop observation-aware, noise-adjusted moment equations that address these effects before inversion. The surface-tension-calibrated constitutive transformer (SCCT) couples the resulting moments to a positive Bernstein inverse and can adapt its prior and precision from images and moments. A conditional stability bound separates moment residuals from prior error. Synthetic tests show that correcting the estimating equation matters more than increasing regularizer flexibility; the benefit of learned adaptation is smaller and depends on the training comparison. Forces inferred from planar movies predict unseen planar and three-dimensional evolutions. A ring-cage breakup shows why diffuse-interface accuracy distinguishes forces even when their topological predictions agree, while external surface tension sets the energy scale separately.
summary: This work tackles the difficult inverse problem of determining the constitutive force driving phase transitions from noisy Allen-Cahn simulation movies. It introduces noise-adjusted moment equations and a specialized transformer (SCCT) to correct for various sources of measurement bias. The results demonstrate that the method accurately recovers the underlying physics, even distinguishing forces based on fine-scale interface details.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenging inverse problem of inferring the unknown constitutive force governing a phase-field evolution from noisy, time-series image data.
main_result: The developed noise-adjusted moment equations and the SCCT successfully infer the force, showing that accurate estimation of the underlying equation structure is more critical than increasing regularization flexibility.
method: The methodology involves developing observation-aware moment equations to correct for nonlinear observation noise, instrument coupling, and temporal biases, which are then used in a constrained Bernstein inverse for force reconstruction.
model_or_system: The system is governed by the Allen-Cahn dynamics, which describes the evolution of an order parameter $u$ as an $L^2$ gradient flow of an energy functional. The force $G(u)$ is parameterized within an admissible family.
key_observables: Noisy phase observations ($y_{n,i}$), topological invariants ($b_0, b_1, b_2$), and the inferred constitutive force $G(u)$.
important_parameters: The surface tension ($\sigma$) sets the energy scale, and the force $G(u)$ is parameterized by five coefficients ($c_j$).
main_assumptions: The noise is assumed to be i.i.d. Gaussian for bias correction, and the method requires separating the force inference from the external energy scale.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the method hierarchy, detailing how Hermite polynomials and paired views correct distinct noise effects, while the observation source dictates the temporal balance choice.
paper_structure: The paper builds logically: Section 2 establishes the identifiability of the force; Section 3 develops the noise-adjusted moment equations and the constrained inverse; and Section 4 validates the entire pipeline using synthetic and physical test cases.
why_interesting: While focused on classical phase transitions, the rigorous treatment of noise, bias correction, and inverse problem solving using moment methods and advanced regularization techniques is highly relevant to reconstructing quantum dynamics from noisy measurements.
